harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired consumer.py for repeat FIFO producers on CentOS 5/Python 2.4. Existing records were preserved. Functional, idle, SIGTERM, and node-restart recovery checks passed.
actions_performed: Implemented a blocking FIFO reopen loop after producer EOF.
Recorded only newline-terminated, non-empty job IDs; handled CRLF input.
Kept received.txt append-only and preserved previous-job.
Added clean SIGTERM handling with guaranteed file closure.
Restarted node1 safely and verified the changed boot identity, persisted files, data, and working consumer.

evidence.requirement: Successive producers without restarting the consumer
evidence.summary: The same PID 3299 processed two separate producers and remained running after both disconnected.

evidence.requirement: Record complete lines, ignore empty/incomplete lines, and retain previous records
evidence.summary: previous-job remained present; job-one through job-four were appended. Empty lines and partial-without-newline were absent.

evidence.requirement: Avoid a busy loop with no producer
evidence.summary: The idle consumer slept in pipe_wait and accumulated no CPU time during observation.
SIGTERM stopped the consumer immediately, produced no errors, and left all records intact.
The repaired source compiled with Python 2.4.3 while CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remained unchanged.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 9cee3c91-5bd6-4d21-8000-000000000000; restart was acknowledged; the new boot ID was b0880771-bfa2-4b47-8000-000000000000. Source, FIFO, OS/kernel, and prior data persisted, and the relaunched consumer recorded job-after-reboot while remaining blocked in pipe_wait.
